It is co-anchored by a **58,473 SF Gabe's** (through Dec-2032, three five-year options) and a **32,000 SF Crunch Fitness** (13+ years on site, through Mar-2033, one five-year option), with junior anchors **Aaron's (10,344 SF)** and a **Dollar Tree (11,979 SF) that is still only an LOI**; together those four are 73.5% of revenue. The in-place pro-forma produces **$682,632 of NOI** on **$1,054,058 of effective gross revenue** less **$371,426 of operating expenses**, off **$956,085 of base rent** at a **$7.43/SF weighted average** — anchor rents of $5.75 (Gabe's) and $5.65 (Crunch) sit at or just below CBRE's own $6.00/SF anchor market rent, so they are secure, market-rate income rather than a repricing opportunity. The real story is the **18,983 SF (12.8%) of vacancy spread across 10 in-line suites**: CBRE models a 36-month absorption at $13.00-$19.00/SF inline market rents to carry occupancy from 87.2% to ~99.5% by 2030, which is what drives the advertised **5.88% ten-year NOI CAGR (75.8% NOI growth)**. Two things temper that. First, **$119,215 of the modeled revenue (11.3%) rests on an unexecuted Dollar Tree LOI**, so the true in-place NOI is closer to $563,000 until that lease is signed. Second, **54% of GLA rolls in 2032-2033** when Gabe's and Crunch expire four months apart — squarely in the exit window of a normal hold. The trade area supports the lease-up thesis: **235,192 residents earning a $98,326 average household income** (3-mile: 73,320 people, $102,284 AHHI), growing ~4% through 2030, with 126 townhomes just sold out next door and 45 more under construction. Real estate taxes in the model are the un-reassessed 2026 budget ($83,758, $0.57/SF), and Henrico County will reassess on a sale — underwrite a step-up. Net: a value-add lease-up story in a solid Richmond infill trade area, priced on an NOI that has to be discounted for the LOI and re-cut for the 2032-33 anchor roll.

deals.notes: **Westland Square** is a **62,735 SF, 100%-leased Food Lion-anchored neighborhood center** on Sunset Boulevard (**29,900 VPD**) just off I-26 in West Columbia, South Carolina, directly across from Lexington Medical Center. The anchor carries the deal: **Food Lion occupies 29,000 SF (46.2% of GLA) at $7.75/SF** — at CBRE's own $8.00/SF grocer market rent — and reports **$690 PSF of sales against a 1.44% health ratio**, roughly $20 million out of a 29,000 SF box. That is exceptional grocer productivity and about the most defensible income in the Evergreen portfolio; the lease runs to December 2032. Ownership recently executed a **10-year AutoZone lease (9,375 SF at $6.50/SF, through May 2036, with 20 years of option control)**, adding an investment-grade credit and roughly $87,000 of annual revenue. The in-place pro-forma shows **$542,984 of NOI** on $735,720 of effective gross revenue less $192,736 of operating expenses. Two figures in the OM do not reconcile and both need to be resolved before pricing: page 2 headlines in-place NOI at **$535,784** versus the pro-forma's **$542,984**, and the pro-forma's printed totals ($563,664 base rent / $172,056 recoveries) exceed the sum of its own twelve printed tenant rows by **$8,010 of base rent and $3,092 of recoveries** — the suite letter 'K' is skipped on both the site plan and the rent roll, so a row appears to be missing from the presentation. The shop row is where the risk sits. The OM markets a **72.4% renewal spread on $2.89 Dry Cleaners** (from $11.50 to ~$19/SF) as proof of mark-to-market, but that tenant reports **$65 PSF of sales and a 33.75% occupancy cost** — an unsustainable ratio, which makes the new rent a default risk rather than evidence of market. Pho & Banh Mi's 13.00% ratio on $96 PSF sales is similarly stretched. The trade area is deep — **293,651 residents at a $94,809 average household income** with ~14.8% projected income growth (3-mile: 53,449 people, $83,552 AHHI) — and roughly 12% of GLA rolls near-term against shop market rents of $12-$20/SF versus $9-$16/SF in place, which is the genuine value-add. Net: a small, well-located grocery box with a superb anchor, a credit-tenant addition and a real mark-to-market case, wrapped in an OM whose own arithmetic needs a correction from the broker.

deals.notes: **Crockett Square** is a **107,122 SF, 100%-leased community center** on US 25E (S Davy Crockett Parkway) in Morristown, Tennessee, 35 miles from Knoxville, shadow-anchored by a **corporately owned Walmart Supercenter** and one-half mile from College Square Mall, the #3 most-visited enclosed mall in the state. The rent roll is four national tenants and nothing else: **Hobby Lobby (58,935 SF, $7.25/SF)**, **Ross Dress for Less (30,187 SF, $12.75)**, **Dollar Tree (10,000 SF, $10.00)** and **Shoe Station (8,000 SF, $14.50)**. Hobby Lobby, Ross and Dollar Tree are original tenants at 21 years' tenure and Hobby Lobby and Ross each exercised a five-year option within the last two years; the OM reports **89% of EGI from original tenants** and a 20-year average tenure. In-place economics are clean and tie out exactly: **$1,028,163 of base rent** ($9.60/SF weighted average) plus **$247,494 of recoveries** for $1,275,657 of effective gross revenue, less $313,795 of operating expenses, for **$961,861 of NOI**. Hobby Lobby reports **$142 PSF of sales at a 7% occupancy cost** — healthy for a craft box — and CBRE puts market rent at **$13.00/SF**, so three of the four leases are 10%-44% below market. Per KPR's standing read, that below-market rent is **secure, sticky income rather than capturable upside**: these tenants will not walk from rents this cheap, and the options are what keep them locked. The corollary is that the income does not grow much either — the OM models a **2.15% ten-year NOI CAGR**. The real exposure is binary rollover in a four-tenant building: **WALT is ±3.6 years**, Shoe Station rolls January 2028, and **Hobby Lobby and Dollar Tree (64.4% of GLA) both expire in September 2030**, with Ross following in January 2031 — effectively the entire center inside four years. Shoe Station is also the one tenant above market ($14.50 vs $13.00) at the earliest expiry. The trade area is modest — **108,129 residents in the true trade area at a $76,961 average household income** (3-mile: 28,056 people, $61,870 AHHI) — but supply is genuinely constrained (the OM notes area topography makes new centers unlikely), 51% of visitors come from more than seven miles away, and TDOT's $67 million 25E/11E interchange project is under construction one mile north. A thin, lower-income trade area of this kind argues for cap-rate cushion rather than aggressive rent-growth assumptions.

deals.notes: **Port Crossing Shopping Center** is a **65,365 SF, 100%-occupied Food Lion-anchored neighborhood center** at Port Republic Road (14,500 AADT) and Neff Avenue in Harrisonburg, Virginia — directly adjacent to **James Madison University (23,000 students)** and across from JMU's Sentara Park, one-half mile from I-81. **Food Lion is the deal**: 45,000 SF (68.8% of GLA, 60.2% of revenue) at **$12.08/SF**, with OM-stated sales of **$15.8 million ($351 PSF)** and ±760.1K annual visits — the chain's busiest store within 10 miles of four — for a **4.38% occupancy cost** including recoveries. It has anchored the center since its 1999 development, with term to **May 2029** and two five-year options. The seven-tenant shop row is a Virginia ABC store (**$2.4 million / $660 PSF of sales**, 4.0% occupancy cost, state-agency credit) plus local restaurants and services. In-place economics: **$891,806 of base rent** ($13.64/SF weighted average) plus **$256,037 of recoveries** and $3,000 of miscellaneous income for **$1,150,843 of effective gross revenue**, less $307,392 of operating expenses, for **$843,451 of NOI**. Rents are almost uniformly **at CBRE's own market assumptions** — Food Lion $12.08 against $12.25, Vietopia $24.99 against $25.00, Madison Nails $25.63 against $25.00, Bobo Cafe $19.58 against $20.00 — which is why the OM only models a **1.87% ten-year NOI CAGR**. There is no meaningful mark-to-market in either direction here; the return has to come from the going-in yield and the trade area. The dominant risk is term. **WALT is ±2.4 years, the shortest in the Evergreen portfolio**: Vito's Italian Kitchen rolls April 2027, You Made It June 2028, Bobo Cafe October 2028, and then Food Lion itself in **May 2029**, inside almost any hold period. A grocer renewal at 60% of revenue is the single decision that determines this asset's value, and the OM also discloses that Food Lion holds a right — exercisable every five years — to **expand its premises by 10,560 SF**, which would displace shop tenants; that clause needs to be read from the lease. The demand story is genuinely strong: **70,364 residents in the true trade area at a $110,489 average household income** (3-mile: 60,013 people, $94,490 AHHI), roughly 70% of JMU students living off campus, a 376-unit apartment project behind the property and a 460-bed student-housing project next door, plus Sentara RMH Medical Center 1.5 miles away and Massanutten Resort's ±1.4 million annual visitors ten miles out. A dense, high-income, supply-constrained college trade area of this kind supports both the in-place rents and a tighter going-in cap — but not without pricing the 2029 grocer renewal.

deals.notes: **Village of Martinsville** is a **288,254 SF, 99.6%-leased grocery-anchored power center** on Commonwealth Boulevard West (**12,900 AADT**), Martinsville's primary commercial corridor, ten miles north of the North Carolina line and six miles from NASCAR's Martinsville Speedway. It is the dominant retail node in its market, with ±2.8 million annual customer visits. The anchor lineup is unusually deep for a market this size: a **55,969 SF Kroger with fuel station** (30-year history, **$39 million / $697 PSF of anecdotal sales**, busiest grocer within 15 miles of 17, six five-year options), **Belk (85,000 SF)**, **Marshalls (24,100 SF, $10.2 million / $423 PSF of sales)**, **Dunham's Sports (43,872 SF, $2.7 million)** and **Harbor Freight (15,338 SF)**, with **83.7% of revenue from national credit tenants** and a **21.4-year average tenure**. Leasing has been active — over 32,000 SF signed since 2025, including **Five Below (14,957 SF, RCD September 2026)**, **Rack Room Shoes** and **Petsense**. In-place economics: **$2,357,414 of base rent** ($8.21/SF weighted average) plus **$405,420 of recoveries** for $2,762,835 of effective gross revenue, less $700,218 of operating expenses, for **$2,062,617 of NOI** — a clean tie-out, with only 1,200 SF vacant. Rents sit at or below CBRE's market assumptions almost everywhere (Kroger $10.27 vs $10.50, Marshalls $8.00 vs $10.75, Dunham's $5.95 vs $7.50, Harbor Freight $10.50 vs $10.75), which per KPR's standing read is **secure, sticky income rather than capturable upside**. The exception that defines the deal is **Belk: 29.5% of GLA at $2.94/SF against an $8.00/SF market**, with option control running to **2037**. That rent is far too cheap for Belk to walk away from, so the income is durable — but a dominant anchor locked at roughly a third of market rent for another decade also caps the center's income growth and its exit value, and Belk's **$49 PSF of sales at a 7.51% occupancy cost** is weak productivity even at that rent. Term is the other pressure point: **WALT is ±3.4 years**, and **Belk (Aug-2028) and Marshalls (Oct-2028) — 109,100 SF, 37.9% of GLA — expire within two months of each other**. Marshalls at $423 PSF of sales and a 2.91% occupancy cost is the renewal you want; Belk is the one to plan around. The trade area is the weakest in the Evergreen portfolio — **20,706 residents within three miles at a $63,282 average household income, with population projected to decline slightly through 2030** (55,927 in the true trade area at $68,707). Low density and below-average incomes argue for a meaningful cap-rate cushion and conservative rent-growth assumptions, notwithstanding the strong in-place sales at Kroger and Marshalls.

deals.notes: **Pierpont Centre** is a **111,158 SF, 94.6%-leased community center** at I-68 (27,900 AADT) and Cheat Road (31,300 AADT) in Morgantown, West Virginia, three miles east of West Virginia University — the dominant retail node of the four primary I-68 exits, with ±632,000 SF of retail. It is anchored by a **37,500 SF Price Cutter** (on site since 2000, **$11.7 million / $312 PSF of anecdotal sales**, top 16% of West Virginia grocers, term to Dec-2029 with two five-year options) and a **20,580 SF Michaels** (to Mar-2031, one five-year option), with a new **11,916 SF Five Below** on a 10-year lease to 2035 and a **Dollar Tree**. In-place economics: **$1,136,335 of base rent** ($10.80/SF weighted average) plus **$329,522 of recoveries** and $2,297 of pylon income for $1,468,154 of effective gross revenue, less $358,282 of operating expenses, for **$1,109,872 of NOI**. Ten NAP pads — Lowe's, two hotels, Wendy's, Outback, Ruby Tuesday, Talbots and others — contribute **$38,520 of CAM reimbursements** with no base rent; confirm those reimbursement agreements survive a transfer. Two structural cautions sit inside the in-place number. First, **the pro-forma assumes renewals that the site plan does not show**: Dollar Tree's site-plan expiry is January 2027 but the model carries it to January 2032 (**$78,933, 5.4% of revenue**), and Mail & More is carried to September 2031 against a December 2027 site-plan expiry. Second, the anchor is a **local independent grocer with eight stores**, not national credit — good operator, but no corporate balance sheet behind 28.7% of revenue. The growth case is real but leasing-dependent: **5,969 SF is vacant across three suites** and **24,003 SF (21.6% of GLA) expires during the hold**, which is what produces the modeled **4.21% ten-year NOI CAGR / 37.5% NOI growth** — the strongest in the portfolio. Some of that roll is genuinely below market (Our Family Craft Shop at $10.07 against a $14.50 market, Michaels at $8.00 against $9.50), but a cluster of shop rents is **above** CBRE's own market — Eye to Eye Optical at $25.74 vs $20.00, Honey Baked Ham at $23.58 vs $18.50, Comcast at $20.54 vs $18.50 — with no sales disclosed, so those renewals are downside risk rather than upside. The trade area is the most affluent in the Evergreen portfolio: **103,669 residents at a $102,287 average household income** (3-mile: 30,781 people, $107,643 AHHI), bordering the Cheat Lake community at a **$187,038 average household income**, with WVU and WVU Medicine driving employment. Density plus income of that quality supports the in-place rents and a tighter going-in cap than a typical secondary-market center.
keyAssumptions: Roster and financials are the OM's In-Place Pro-Forma (page 9), stated on a CY-2027 basis (Jan-27 to Dec-27 contractual rent and recoveries, no general vacancy loss).

THE MODEL ASSUMES OPTION EXERCISES THAT THE SITE PLAN DOES NOT SHOW: Dollar Tree (site plan Jan-2027 vs modeled Jan-2032) and Mail & More (site plan Dec-2027 vs modeled Sep-2031). Together roughly $108,700 of revenue depends on renewals being confirmed from the leases.

WALT is carried at the OM's stated ±3.7 years, which is only reproducible with Dollar Tree expiring Jan-2027. The roster's own (pro-forma) expiries roll up to 4.1 years SF-weighted as of 01/01/27 — the gap is exactly the Dollar Tree renewal the income model assumes.

Ten NAP parcels (Lowe's, two hotels, Wendy's, Outback, Ruby Tuesday, Talbots, Clear Mountain Bank, BF's, Los Mariachis) are carried on the roster with no SF and no base rent; they contribute $38,520 of CAM reimbursement, 11.7% of total recoveries. Their lease dates are modeled 01/01/27-12/31/46 placeholders, not actual terms.
Three vacant suites totaling 5,969 SF (03, 13, 15) are carried at $0 so roster SF ties to the 111,158 SF GLA; CBRE models a 16-month absorption beginning 01/01/27 with first absorption 01/01/28.
Price Cutter's $11.7 million / $312 PSF sales figure is described as ANECDOTAL — unverified by the tenant. Price Cutter is a local independent operator (eight stores), not a national credit.

CBRE's 2027 market rents: $8.50/SF for suite 17, $20.00/SF sub-2,000 SF, $18.50/SF for 2,000-5,000 SF, $14.50/SF for 5,000-7,000 SF, $13.50/SF for suite 11 and $9.50/SF for 20,000+ SF space, all NNN+MF with 3.00% growth; new-lease TI is $35.00/SF.

Real estate taxes are NOT reassessed — they equal the 2026 budget ($94,769). West Virginia assesses at 60% of appraised value and reappraises annually; a sale price above the current appraisal will flow through.
No asking price or cap rate is published in this OM.

redFlags.description: The in-place pro-forma credits renewals the site plan contradicts: Dollar Tree is carried to Jan-2032 (site plan says Jan-2027) at $6.46/SF, and Mail & More to Sep-2031 (site plan says Dec-2027). Roughly $108,700 of revenue — 7.4% of EGI — rests on options that must be confirmed from the leases.

The OM's headline WALT and its NOI use DIFFERENT assumptions for the same lease. Recomputing WALT from the pro-forma's own expiries gives 4.1 years; the OM's stated ±3.7 years is only reproducible if Dollar Tree is treated as expiring January 2027 — i.e. the marketing WALT excludes the renewal that the income statement counts. One of the two is wrong, and the income side is the one that matters.

The anchor is a local independent: Price Cutter operates eight stores in northcentral West Virginia and carries 28.7% of revenue with term only to Dec-2029. Sales are 'anecdotal' ($11.7M / $312 PSF), there is no national credit behind the lease, and grocery in a small market is unforgiving of a weak operator.

21.6% of GLA (24,003 SF) expires during the hold on top of 5,969 SF already vacant — the modeled 4.21% ten-year NOI CAGR depends on re-leasing roughly a quarter of the center at CBRE's market rents with $35.00/SF of new-lease TI.

A cluster of shop rents sits ABOVE the OM's own market assumptions with no sales disclosed — Eye to Eye Optical $25.74 vs $20.00, Honey Baked Ham $23.58 vs $18.50, Comcast $20.54 vs $18.50. Those are mark-to-market DOWNSIDE at their 2029-2031 expiries and they inflate current NOI.

$38,520 of recoveries (11.7% of total) comes from ten NAP parcels the seller does not own, on reimbursement agreements the OM does not describe. Confirm the REA/CAM agreements, their assignability and their expiry before capitalizing that income.
Three vacant suites (2,646, 1,725 and 1,598 SF) require a 16-month absorption; at $35.00/SF of TI plus commissions, lease-up capital is a real drag on early-year cash flow.

Real estate taxes ($94,769) are the un-reassessed 2026 budget. West Virginia reappraises annually at 60% of value, so a sale price above the current appraisal should be expected to flow into the bill.

This is what drives the modeled 37.5% ten-year NOI growth — the highest in the portfolio.

$107,643 average household income within three miles and $187,038 in the adjacent Cheat Lake community, with WVU, WVU Medicine and the dominant I-68 Exit 7 retail node (±632,000 SF) driving traffic. High income plus high density is exactly the profile that supports above-average rents and a tighter cap.

Lowe's (3rd busiest hardware store within 30 miles of 64), WVU Medicine, two hotels and a cluster of national restaurants sit on NAP parcels — the center gets the traffic and $38,520 of CAM reimbursements without carrying the real estate.
Five Below signed a 10-year lease to 2035 at $12.53/SF and Spencer & Kuehn signed in Oct-2025 — evidence that national and regional tenants are still choosing this node.
